ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, legal representatives, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the French asset-freeze list (Gels d'avoirs), OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals list, and UN Security Council consolidated lists. Politically exposed persons must be identified under a risk-based approach pursuant to Article L561-10 CMF; enhanced due diligence applies to UBOs from jurisdictions with strategic AML/CFT deficiencies. Additional screening must verify that alcohol export activities do not breach trade sanctions applicable to target markets.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI, and Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) at registre-national-entreprises.inpi.fr; name pre-reservation is processed by the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The articles of association and all mandatory public filings must be in French. A corporate name may contain foreign-language words, but any non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration and the transliteration must be consistent with the bylaws. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or confuse protected geographical indications applicable to alcoholic beverages.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bourse, Caisse d'Épargne, Caisse des Dépôts
Champagne, Cognac, and other AOC/AOP protected denominations when unsubstantiated
Terms implying military or national-security capacity unless ministry consent is granted
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The pre-incorporation name declaration (Déclaration préalable à l'immatriculation) is valid for eight calendar weeks and may be renewed by filing a new declaration before expiry. If the registry refuses the proposed name, the applicant must first amend the name or provide supporting evidence, then re-file through the INPI formalities portal. A formal refusal may be appealed by filing an application with the supervising judge of the Tribunal de commerce within fifteen days of notification, and further recourse is available before the first-instance commercial court under Articles L.123-36 and R.123-4 of the French Commercial Code.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office through a licensed domiciliation agent is permissible for an SAS engaged in wholesale spirits export, provided the domiciliation company holds a valid prefecture-authorised licence and the registrant executes a formal domiciliation agreement. The company must remain able to maintain statutory records in France; customs and excise authorities may additionally require a fixed operational address for alcohol storage and movement controls.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high probability, estimated at 60% in each 12-month operating cycle, because the entity operates in alcoholic-beverage distribution and is subject to unannounced customs, excise, and tax inspection programmes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) – Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (formation, constitution), Règlement général du Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; online filing portal Guichet Entreprises; service provided by Infogreffe
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) signed by all shareholders; accompanying incorporation dossier containing statutory declarations and Annexes (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SAS has no legal minimum share capital; capital is fixed by the Articles of Association. For cash contributions, at least 50% of the subscribed capital must be paid up upon incorporation, with the remainder payable within five years. Capital funds must be deposited in a blocked special account with a notary, bank, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations until the RCS registration certificate is issued. No mandatory escrow account beyond the depositary requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Articles of Association hereby confirm their respective share subscriptions to the capital of Société par Actions Simplifiée and authorize the deposit of initial paid-up funds with the approved depositary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be fixed at the address in the Articles and notification thereof be given to the RCS. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the President and all other officers named in the Articles be and hereby are appointed to their offices for the statutory term. RESOLVED LASTLY, that the President shall file the incorporation dossier, publish the mandatory legal notice, and submit the declaration of beneficial owners to the competent Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association and Subscribe Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders, advised by a French Avocat or Notary (notary mandatory for contributions of real estate; otherwise private deed sufficient)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Statuts in French or with certified French translation; include corporate form, registered office address, purpose, share capital, share classes, and corporate governance rules. Each shareholder signs the Articles and subscribes shares representing cash contribution. Transfer at least 50% of cash contributions into a blocked deposit account with a licensed depositary (bank, notary, Caisse des Dépôts). Obtain the depositary certificate attesting the deposit.
required_dossiers: Passport or valid ID of each shareholder
Bank depositary receipt / certificate of deposit of capital
If applicable: auditor (commissaire aux comptes) report on contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary refuses to certify or statutory clauses are considered incomplete, the founder may amend the Articles by supplementary shareholders' resolution and resubmit the corrected deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal announcement journal (Journal d'annonces légales) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a mandatory legal notice containing the proposed company name, legal form, registered office, share capital, corporate purpose, duration, and names of officers. Submit the notice to the selected legal gazette; upon publication, obtain the attestation de parution (certificate of publication) to be appended to the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation certificate if any
Proposed articles of association (executed or draft)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is delayed or the legal notice contains errors, publish a corrective notice in the same gazette within 30 days and obtain a new attestation without reopening the statutory timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Declaration of Beneficial Owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – filed jointly with the incorporation application, processed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the 'Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs' form identifying each individual who directly or indirectly holds more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights, or controls the company by other means. Include names, birth details, nationality, address, and nature and extent of control. The declaration is lodged via the Guichet Entreprises portal along with the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Standard beneficial owner declaration form (Formulaire DBE-P)
Proof of identity of each beneficial owner
Supporting resolution or agreement establishing control
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries inaccurate beneficial owner information, submit an amended declaration within 20 days and provide explicit consent to the registry's proposed rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Consolidated Incorporation Dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the single electronic portal Guichet Entreprises (Infogreffe processing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Guichet Entreprises portal, upload the complete incorporation dossier: executed Articles, power of attorney if any, deposit certificate, legal notice attestation, beneficial owner declaration, registered office supporting documents, and officer appointments. Pay the RCS registration fee online. Receive provisional RCS filing reference and process for legal verification.
required_dossiers: Publication attestation from the legal gazette
Bank or depositary certificate of capital deposit
Form of application for registration (M1/M0 equivalents)
Evidence of registered office occupancy (lease or free use authorization)
Notarized powers if using a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or refusal, correct the identified defect and resubmit within the reported deadline (commonly 15 days). Address any judicial substantive objections by filing a brief and requesting a second inspection. The statutory maximum consideration period is 5 business days from full file receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract and Initiate Excise and Post-Registration Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS extract), Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) for alcohol warehousing, and relevant social administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, download the official K-bis extract. Immediately thereafter file the preliminary notice of excise operation with DGDDI (Direction des douanes) to become an approved warehousekeeper or registered consignor/consignee for alcohol excise suspension. Submit mandatory social registration to URSSAF and corporate health and safety declarations.
required_dossiers: Customs form for excise approval (INTP or notice of activity)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If excise approval is delayed, continue under duty-paid procedures while confirming the complete excise file; appeal to the customs director via complaint within two months. For social field delays, coordinate with URSSAF or Infogreffe for rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Industrial Safety and Operational Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP), DREAL (environmental/ICPE), and municipal fire safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an ICPE declaration or registration (if applicable under rubrique 4331 for packaged spirits storage) to DREAL, together with the fire safety protocol for the warehouse and general technical control review. Obtain after approval the standard fire safety certificate and any administrative clearance for storing high-proof beverage alcohol under occupational safety conditions.
required_dossiers: Fire safety dossier (diagnostic, evacuation plan, extinguishing devices)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DREAL or DDPP objects, modify the storage configuration to meet the framed thresholds, submit a corrective plan within 30 days, or apply for a lower ICPE classification tier. Appeals may be lodged with the administrative tribunal (tribunal administratif) within two months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) – Customs and Indirect Taxes Authority; Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DREETS) for occupational compliance; DREAL for environmental installations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'entrepositaire agréé (for excise suspension and export dispatch) – licensed as a Registered Warehousekeeper under the French General Tax Code and Union Customs Code, together with any required ICPE operating permit for the storage of flammable packaged spirits (rubrique 4331)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA is not required for a pure spirits export wholesale activity. A limited ICPE declaration or registration under the 'avec déclaration' regime (rubrique 4331 – alcoholic beverage storage, Category 2 flammable liquids) applies if the total storage quantity exceeds the statutory threshold; otherwise the facility is exempted from ICPE formalities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental code limits: no industrial process wastewater is generated; any cleaning or condensate discharge must meet COD < 300 mg/L and pH 6.5-8.5. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must not exceed 2 g VOCs per liter of stored spirit in suspension. Spill containment pallets and a firewater holding basin must be installed; any release must be contained and reported to the local water authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by a competent commission based on the building's resistance classification; fire containment system and clear emergency evacuation routes are compulsory. A structural load inspection certificate confirms the floor can support the maximum bottle pallet load. Occupational clearance is required from the DREETS to ensure compliance with the French Labour Code (eight-hour ventilation, face-mask provisions, alcohol exposure signage, and emergency response drills). The workplace environment must hold an up-to-date document unique d'évaluation des risques and a valid health and safety register.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP) of the Ministère de l'économie, des finances et de la souveraineté industrielle et numérique, official portal www.impots.gouv.fr with the 'Espace Professionnel' for corporate income tax and VAT (CA3) filing; company formation and TIN attribution operate through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and alcohol excise are administered separately by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI), portal www.douane.gouv.fr; EU VAT number validation via the VIES database (europa.eu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the SAS incorporation through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, mandatory since 1 January 2023), which automatically delivers the SIREN/SIRET business identifiers. Step 2: DGFiP then allocates the French intra-Community VAT number in the format FR + 2 control digits + SIREN; this VAT number is the statutory TIN for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll and local taxes, and must be verified in the VIES database before use in intra-EU transactions. Step 3: Obtain an EORI number (FR + SIREN) from DGDDI for customs declarations and, because the activity is wholesale distribution of high-proof sorghum baijiu (ISIC 4632 / HS 2208.90), obtain DGDDI approval as an excise operator (entrepositaire agréé or registered consignor) to export alcohol under duty suspension with the DAE excise document. Step 4: A foreign entity without a French business presence cannot obtain a French VAT number directly; it must appoint an accredited fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) under CGI Article 289 A and file form 1544-SD with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères, or use the EU OSS/IOSS special schemes; the French SAS vehicle is established and therefore files directly with its local service des impôts des entreprises (SIE).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) operating jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the banking resolution and licensing authority. The Banque de France holds exclusive power over balance-of-payments statistics, cross-border payment declarations, and euro wholesale settlement (TARGET2).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a eurozone member, maintains full convertibility of the euro for current account and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles L.411-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code. There is no general exchange-control authorization required for an SAS to receive capital injections, pay foreign suppliers, or remit dividends to a Chinese parent. Profit distribution hurdles are tax-driven rather than FX-driven: dividends sourced in France to a Chinese resident beneficial owner are subject to withholding tax of 10%, reduced to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the SAS capital and meets the treaty anti-abuse and substance conditions in Article 10 of the France-China double tax treaty. The CNY is not freely convertible onshore; the SAS must use EUR, CNH offshore, or convertible USD settlement lanes for all France-side flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, mandated conversion ratio, or required conversion timeline applies in France; exporters may retain foreign currency balances in licensed banks. The relevant mandatory obligation is statistical reporting: each cross-border payment equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 must be reported to the Banque de France by the servicing bank under EU Regulation ECB/2018/2317 and the French arrêté of 13 January 2020. For goods exporting, invoices must be matched to customs declarations (DX7) with the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), and the complete remittance evidence file must be retained for five years for AML/CFT and customs audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte courant) plus blocked Capital Escrow Account for share capital placement
Operational Account plus Documentary Letter of Credit (MT700) and trade finance facilities
Multi-currency treasury account (EUR/CNH/USD) with Asia-Pacific corridor coverage

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. / Crédit Agricole CIB
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Escrow Account and Commercial Import Settlement Facility
Operational Account and Treasury/FX Hedging Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict limitations. A French-licensed or EU-passported EMI (e.g., Qonto, Revolut Business, Payoneer) can support day-to-day operational euro flows, invoice payments, and low-value cross-border transfers below EUR 250,000 monthly, and may open accounts remotely. However, EMIs generally cannot originate documentary Letters of Credit, execute EUR/CNH delivery-versus-payment trade settlement, or interface with the DGDDI excise (accises) payment module required for high-proof Baijiu importation. Legal constraints require the EMI to hold a valid ACPR payment-services licence or EU passport, subject the entity to full RBE and UBO KYC, and apply sanctions screening to every beneficiary; alcohol excise duty payments must always be routed through a full-service credit institution. The EMI rail is therefore viable only as an auxiliary operating account, not as the principal import settlement and capital custody rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not mandate physical appearance of all directors for a standard-risk wholesale distribution SAS; remote opening is permitted when the entity has a completed RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing, apostilled and legalised corporate documents, and a successful video KYC interview of at least one director and the beneficial owner. Tier 1 banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale) nevertheless require one in-person signature session at a Paris branch for the authorised signatory, principally to validate the EUR 12,500+ wire approval mandate; HSBC Continental Europe and digital-first institutions accept a fully remote hybrid flow. Expected onboarding timeline is 4-6 weeks for Tier 1 banks, inclusive of compliance interviews, UBO chain verification, and registration of the corporate banking mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Importation of excise-controlled alcohol (Chinese Baijiu) from a non-EU origin, creating suspicion of smuggling, duty evasion, or diversion from bonded warehousing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid French import licence for spirituous beverages (licence d'importation), the SAS wholesale licence (licence de vente en gros), DGDDI registration as a declared excise trader, approved bonded or customs-authorised warehouse arrangement, complete customs declarations (DX7 / IMO), batch-level provenance files from the Chinese distillery, customs duty payment receipts, executed supply agreements, and an independent logistics audit certificate proving every batch physically entered EU customs territory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Chinese corporate ownership with unidentified layers or artificial ownership cascade; bank cannot verify the ultimate beneficial owner chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled RBE form filed with the Commercial Court registry, UBO chain chart signed by the statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes), SAMR incorporation certificates for each parent entity, Chinese tax registration certificates, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent evidencing economic substance (staff, premises, Baijiu brand ownership), bank reference letters from the parent's clearing bank, and a recorded video interview of the UBO confirming the commercial rationale for the French distribution entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inter-company flows raising potential round-tripping, artificial commission, or cross-border layering between the SAS, the Chinese supplier, and distribution customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed international distribution agreement, OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation for the distribution functions and intercompany remuneration, detailed commercial invoices with unique sequential reference numbers, full logistics file (bill of lading, CMR, freight invoices, customs release notices), a twelve-month projected treasury flow model, and written confirmation that all customer proceeds are recovered from independent third-party retailers and wholesalers without parent offsetting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single lump-sum capital injection followed by rapid outbound disbursement to third-party foreign beneficiaries, triggering a cash-flow anomaly and potential money-laundering alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified shareholder resolution approving the capital contribution (apport en capital), notarial deed and RBE registration certificate, statutory purpose code on the incoming SWIFT wire (INVCAP-CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION), source-of-funds statement from the shareholder's Chinese bank, contractual delivery schedules for each supplier payment, and the bank's own compliance sign-off on expected transaction patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SAS used as a payment routing vehicle for alcohol goods that may not physically enter France, creating a 'paper importer' risk pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party logistics warehouse receiving reports, DGDDI customs release notifications in the name of the SAS, stock inventory certificates signed by the in-house accountant, VAT and INTRASTAT filings showing French VIES presence, customs broker engagement letter, first-import pilot report, and a physical stock certificate prepared by an external auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections from the Chinese shareholder must first clear China's SAFE ODI registration and outward remittance filing, then be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 in EUR (converted from CNY/CNH) or directly in CNH to the French SAS account. The wire must carry the Chinese remittance purpose code for outbound direct investment and a Bank-to-Beneficiary narrative reading 'INVESTMENT CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - APPORTS EN CAPITAL SAS' referencing the notarial deed and RBE record. On the French side, the servicing bank receives the transfer through TARGET2, files the Banque de France cross-border declaration where the value exceeds EUR 12,500, and temporarily places the funds in the blocked Capital Escrow Account until the SAS incorporation and Commercial Registry registration (greffe du tribunal de commerce) are formally evidenced. After release, the treasury is moved onto the operational account with documented source-of-funds chain. No intermediary shell bank should be used; the settlement should remain within SEPA/EUR T2 rails for full compliance traceability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlements to Chinese Baijiu distilleries and freight forwarders are cleared through three permitted rails: (i) direct SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the SAS EUR or CNH account to the supplier's account at a Chinese bank or its EU correspondent; (ii) documentary commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) opened on behalf of the SAS, payable against presentation of the commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, customs export/import declarations, certificate of origin, insurance policy, and EU conformity statement, with documents examined by the advising bank under UCP 600; and (iii) optional CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) settlement for CNY-denominated payments where both counterparties maintain CIPS member accounts. Every outbound disbursement must be screened against EU sanctions (EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC, UN) and, where above EUR 12,500, is reported by the bank to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. Excise duty payments to the DGDDI are executed through the secured customs electronic payment module (SIGAL/Comp@ct) linked to the same liquidity account, with automatic debit authority granted to the customs administration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign-exchange contracts (change à terme or deliverable forwards) on EUR/CNH and EUR/USD up to 12 months tenor, permitted only against documented import/export commitments and executed under the EMIR non-financial-counterparty hedging exemption.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on onshore CNY (USD/CNY reference rate via CFETS fixing) when physical CNH settlement is commercially unavailable, conditional on an underlying China-import commitment and the bank's market-risk approval through the ACPR framework.

Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps / EUR-CNH cross-currency swaps) for maturities beyond 12 months used to hedge the foreign-currency exposure on shareholder loans, purchase payments, and future dividend remittances, settled through TARGET2 with full collateralisation.

Zero-premium FX option collars on EUR/CNH packaged by the bank's markets desk; permissible where the SAS qualifies as a professional client under MIFID II and the board has approved a written treasury hedging policy with utilisation limits.

Spot EUR/CNH and EUR/USD transactions (T+2) executed against identified underlying commercial flows, limited to not more than 10% of the annual cleared trade value and subject to the bank's markets-conduct and suitability controls.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) including balance sheet, profit and loss statement, and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce, transmitted through the INPI Single Formalities Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year close; where accounts are approved at a later date, the filing must be made within one month of that approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered fine up to Euro 5,000 for the legal representative if the filing obligation is not completed; continued failure after formal notice may lead to suspension of payments to shareholders and administrative strike-off from the Trade and Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultat n°2065) and general tax annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus three months; for calendar-year entities the return is due by the filing deadline set by the tax administration, generally 30 April following the close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of 10% of assessed corporate tax, increased to 20% after a formal demand, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%; persistent non-filing can lead to ex officio tax assessment and enforcement, but not directly to corporate strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner (UBO) register confirmation and effective-owner declaration update in connection with any share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, operated by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; an annual confirmation must be certified when the company’s annual accounts are filed with the trade registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the UBO declaration incurs a fine of Euro 750 per non-declared beneficiary and may suspend voting and dividend rights; continued non-disclosure can expose directors to reputational and administrative sanctions but not direct strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual register maintenance declaration confirming registered office, legal representation and statutory data of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce via the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change is filed within 30 days; if no change occurs, the annual filing of financial statements serves as the annual confirmation of register data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or omitted register declarations expose the legal representative to a fine up to Euro 1,500 and can constitute grounds for judicial strike-off from the RCS if an inactive company remains non-compliant.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor must be appointed when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total balance sheet above Euro 5,000,000, net turnover above Euro 10,000,000, or at least 50 permanent employees on average; any SAS that has consolidated subsidiaries may nonetheless be audited under group requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation 2014-03), which incorporates EU accounting directives; IFRS is permitted for consolidated accounts but not for the statutory separate financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A share transfer in the SAS must be reported through an updated UBO declaration to INPI within 15 calendar days. The company must also re-confirm the accuracy of its beneficial-owner registration when the annual accounts are deposited; any undisclosed transfer is a continuing offence and the affected shareholder's voting and dividend rights may be suspended until the declaration is corrected.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Securities Movements (registre des actions et des mouvements de titres)
Decisions and Minutes Ledger (registre des procès-verbaux et décisions de l'associé unique)
Director and Officer Record (registre des mandats sociaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 1,300 per annum for commercial domiciliation, registered-office and mail-handling services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 20,000 per audit cycle for a mid-size SAS with export activities

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply 15% to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for a 12-month period; the company must generally have turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% of its capital held by individuals or qualifying companies meeting the ownership condition.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% SME rate applies only to qualifying profit within the EUR 42,500 band; the 25% rate applies above it. There is no general tax holiday for a French SAS. Eligibility for sectoral or regional incentives must be established separately. A French parent may, subject to statutory conditions, apply the participation exemption to qualifying dividends, generally leaving a 5% add-back for expenses and charges; the French tax-consolidation regime is available only where its ownership and other conditions are met.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to an annual deduction cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The schema's five-year value does not describe the French general rule. Loss carryback is generally available for one year, subject to a EUR 1 million cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), with applicable 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD financial-statement schedules and other required annexes, filed electronically through the professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr using EDI-TDFC or EFI where available. Form 2572-SD is used for the IS balance payment; forms 2571-SD concern installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly IS installments generally apply during the financial year, subject to statutory exemptions. A company with a calendar-year financial year normally pays installments on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with the balance paid by the applicable return-payment deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the financial year-end. For a financial year ending 31 December, the return is generally due on the second business day after 1 May of the following year. The IS balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; for a 31 December year-end, it is generally due 15 May. Confirm the applicable year's administration deadline and any announced extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS's legal name, SIREN, registered address, activity, tax office, financial-year opening and closing dates, and applicable filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder does not replace the French SAS as taxpayer. Report the French company's own identifiers and French financial year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable result and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the result determined under French tax rules, reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit, apply available deductions and loss carryforwards within statutory limits, calculate IS at the applicable rate, and report credits and reductions with supporting forms.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SAS's French-taxable business income. A foreign shareholder's residence does not exempt the SAS's French profits from French IS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the required balance sheet, profit and loss account, fixed-asset, depreciation, provisions, equity, tax reconciliation, and other financial and tax schedules applicable to the company's accounts and transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use French statutory accounting and tax classifications. Disclose related-party dealings and foreign-currency amounts using applicable French accounting and tax rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile IS installments and credits against the final IS liability and pay any balance by the statutory payment deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is made by the French SAS through the applicable French professional tax account; a non-resident shareholder is not the filing taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay required quarterly IS installments, subject to the applicable thresholds, exemptions, and first-year rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess installments using the French SAS's own liability and prior-year tax position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the annual transfer-pricing declaration when the company falls within the statutory scope, including applicable information about the group, controlled transactions, and transfer-pricing policy.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS within scope reports relevant cross-border transactions with associated enterprises, including transactions with its foreign shareholder or group companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2067-SD, statement of general expenses, where applicable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report specified categories of general expenses when the statutory filing conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same French filing thresholds to the SAS; do not omit reportable expenses solely because a recipient or shareholder is non-resident.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% after formal notice remains unanswered within the prescribed period and to 80% in cases such as discovered concealed activity or fraudulent conduct. Late payment generally bears interest at 0.20% per month and may attract a 5% collection surcharge. Inaccurate or incomplete returns can trigger additional penalties, commonly 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres, subject to the facts and statutory procedure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French SAS to a non-resident corporate shareholder, the domestic withholding rate is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The French domestic exemption for qualifying EU/EEA parent companies may apply if statutory ownership, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. For an eligible Chinese corporate beneficial owner, the France-China income tax treaty generally limits withholding to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the payer's capital, and 10% in other qualifying cases. Different domestic rules apply to individual recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Establish the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, qualifying direct shareholding, and entitlement under the applicable treaty and anti-abuse rules. Obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent tax authority. Submit the applicable French treaty-relief forms and supporting documents to the French payer or competent French tax office before payment where advance relief is available; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and claim a refund within the applicable limitation period. Retain the residence certificate, ownership evidence, dividend resolution, payment records, and beneficial-ownership analysis. Relief is not automatic merely because a recipient provides a certificate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties and other specified French-source income paid to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to the income's legal characterization, exemptions, and treaty relief. France-China treaty royalties are generally limited to 10% of the gross amount for a qualifying beneficial owner. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding under ordinary domestic rules, but exceptions apply, including payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions; the France-China treaty generally permits source-country taxation of qualifying interest at a maximum 10%. Confirm that the payment is genuine interest or royalty, that the recipient is the beneficial owner, and that anti-abuse and documentation requirements are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French full transfer-pricing documentation under Article L.13 AA of the Tax Procedures Code generally applies where the French entity or relevant group meets a statutory threshold, including annual turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 150 million, or specified group-ownership or control conditions involving an entity meeting that threshold. The annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration (Form 2257-SD) generally applies at a lower EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or where a qualifying group relationship brings the company within scope. Separate documentation obligations can apply below these thresholds under general audit rules; confirm current statutory scope and related-party transaction requirements.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. French tax outcomes remain subject to transfer-pricing requirements, the general anti-abuse rule, abuse-of-law doctrine, beneficial-ownership analysis, substance-over-form principles, and applicable anti-hybrid and controlled-foreign-company rules. The SAS should maintain actual decision-making, personnel, premises, functions, assets, and risk-control evidence proportionate to its claimed commercial role. A baijiu import and wholesale business should document inventory ownership, pricing, customs valuation, credit and foreign-exchange risks, and the allocation of marketing, logistics, and regulatory functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion or fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales or inventory, maintaining false books, fabricating expenses, submitting materially false returns, or deliberately omitting taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, surcharges generally up to 80% in aggravated cases, and criminal prosecution where statutory fraud elements are met. Tax fraud can carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of EUR 500,000, increased to seven years and EUR 3 million in specified aggravated circumstances; additional penalties may apply under the Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability for their own participation, civil liability where statutory conditions are met, and tax-responsibility proceedings for fraudulent or serious and repeated tax non-compliance. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax penalty; any restriction requires a separate lawful judicial or enforcement basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undeclared related-party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing baijiu, services, financing, trademarks, or other transactions with related parties outside the arm's-length principle; failing to provide required documentation; or using an artificial structure to shift French profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, interest, applicable tax surcharges, and a specific documentation penalty generally equal to the greater of EUR 10,000 or 5% of the reassessed profits connected with undocumented transactions, subject to statutory conditions and the applicable version of the law. Failure to file a required Form 2257-SD can incur a separate penalty, generally EUR 150 per omitted or inaccurate item, subject to statutory caps and rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for deliberate participation in fraud or for statutory tax-responsibility grounds. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not automatically pierce the corporate veil or create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Concealed permanent establishment or artificial non-resident arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming that French sales, personnel, management, or operational functions are outside France when a French taxable presence exists, or interposing an entity without genuine commercial functions to obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of French tax on attributable profits, interest, surcharges, and possible penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct; treaty relief may be denied under beneficial-ownership, principal-purpose, or domestic anti-abuse rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability depends on individual participation, statutory tax-responsibility grounds, or separate civil or criminal findings; it is not automatic merely because an entity is found to have a French taxable presence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful dividend distribution or withholding-tax non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without required corporate approvals or distributable reserves, applying an unsupported treaty rate, failing to withhold or remit tax, or mischaracterizing a distribution as interest or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, applicable surcharges, and potential penalties for inaccurate declarations or deliberate concealment. Invalid or unlawful distributions may also be subject to corporate-law remedies and repayment claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or criminal liability for knowingly authorizing unlawful distributions, fraud, or failure to comply with statutory duties. Personal liability is fact-specific and is not an automatic consequence of a withholding-tax reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Alcohol excise, customs, and market-access non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing or placing baijiu on the French market without required excise and customs treatment, registrations, guarantees, movement documentation, product-compliance measures, or applicable alcohol-trade authorization; misdeclaring origin, classification, value, or alcohol strength.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs and excise assessments, seizure or forfeiture, interest, administrative fines, and potential criminal penalties under applicable customs, excise, and alcohol-trade legislation. The exact consequence depends on the breached obligation, goods, intent, and applicable procedure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal administrative or criminal exposure for their own unlawful acts or statutory responsibilities. Corporate limited liability does not shield an individual from personal criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, sanctions, or suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing beneficial ownership or the source of funds, accepting unexplained third-party payments, circumventing sanctions, falsifying trade or shipping documents, or failing to meet applicable anti-money-laundering and reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential account restrictions, transaction blocking, confiscation, regulatory or customs penalties, and criminal prosecution. Money laundering can carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of EUR 375,000, with higher penalties for aggravated conduct; sanctions breaches may attract separate severe penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may be criminally liable for knowing participation, facilitation, or specified failures in their own duties. Travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment require the relevant statutory or judicial basis and are not automatic consequences of a compliance breach.
